sense: an explanation of what something means

evidence: Plin. NH 7.203: ostentōrum et somniōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The explaining of laws, dreams, signs and words; also a translation (see translate).

terms.gloss: interpret, explain; understand (a thing in a certain way)
evidence: Cic. Off. 2.5: sī interpretārī velīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From interpres, a go-between or interpreter: to explain, and also to take a thing in a certain sense (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: take (a remark) in a certain way
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with in or ad + accusative
evidence: Ter. Ad. 606: ad contumēliam omnia accipiunt magis
Ter. Eun. 875: in eam partem accipiōque
terms.comment: The everyday way of saying how something is understood: to take it as an insult, ad contumēliam accipere; in that sense, in eam partem.

phrases.english: Explain an insult and you make it sharper.

phrases.latin: nec quicquam aliud est philosophia, sī interpretārī velīs, quam studium sapientiae
phrases.english: and philosophy, if you want to put it in other words, is nothing but the pursuit of wisdom

phrases.latin: omnēs, quibus rēs sunt minus secundae, magis sunt nesciō quōmodo suspīciōsī; ad contumēliam omnia accipiunt magis
phrases.english: all those whose affairs are going badly are somehow more suspicious; they take everything more as an insult

sources: Lewis & Short: interpretatio · Lewis & Short: interpretor · Lewis & Short: accipio
